details.title: Discrete Entropy: Choice, Uncertainty and Bits
details.idea: Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution is H = -sum_i p_i log2 p_i bits, where each outcome contributes its probability times its own surprise log2(1/p_i).
details.audience: A second-year engineering undergraduate comfortable with logarithms and elementary probability

details.plan: Learners edit up to six outcome probabilities and see each outcome's surprise-and-weight contribution plus the total Shannon entropy in bits. Because inputs are weights rather than fixed probabilities, the page normalizes them, which also handles zero weights cleanly. Comparing a one-hot distribution with an equally likely one shows certainty at zero bits and maximum uncertainty at log2 n bits.
